title: How Latin America Is Climbing the High-Tech Value Chain
gist: A J.P. Morgan Private Bank LatAm strategist and an AQ editor argue Latin America is climbing the high-tech value chain: Mexico's advanced-tech exports to the US reached $98.3 billion, Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic build chip workforces, and Brazil leads a data center boom.

insights.claim: Mexico's advanced technology exports to the US grew 47% annually to $98.3 billion, making it the leading exporter last year, ahead of Taiwan, though Taiwan retook the lead in the first half of this year.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Confirms nearshoring is moving into high-value electronics; track monthly Census trade data.
insights.locator: Last year, Mexico became the leading exporter

insights.claim: The US depends on Mexico for 40% of its server center imports, which are essential to AI development.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: AI hardware supply-chain exposure to Mexico is material and tariff-sensitive.
insights.locator: As a result, the U.S. now depends on Mexico

insights.claim: Foxconn is building what could be the world's largest assembly facility for Nvidia GB200 superchips in Guadalajara, and other Taiwanese ODMs are investing heavily on both sides of the border.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Direct read-through for Nvidia server supply chain and Mexican industrial real estate.

themes.theme: Moving up the chip value chain

insights.claim: Assembly, testing and packaging (ATP) is the lowest-value step in chipmaking, so Mexico's policy also emphasizes design of mature chips used in cars, toasters and subway doors rather than cutting-edge ones.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Value capture requires design, not just assembly; watch if the policy converts.
insights.locator: But ATP is the lowest-value step

insights.claim: Design facilities need far less capital than ATP: about $200,000 versus $2-10 million, so the binding constraint is workforce training and R&D funding.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Capital is not the bottleneck; talent pipelines are.

insights.claim: Mexico's Kutsari initiative works with universities on training and with legal reforms on patents, IP and red tape to boost chip competitiveness.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Policy program to monitor for execution.
insights.locator: To address this, Mexico is building out Kutsari

themes.theme: Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic

insights.claim: Costa Rica's Centers of Excellence program, with over $45 million committed by Costa Rican and US companies, trains students with multinational-designed curricula for ATP certification; medical devices are about 40% of exports.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN

insights.claim: Intel announced it would shut down its chip center in Costa Rica in favor of Vietnam, though at least a dozen other companies still operate in the field.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Shows the region still competes with Asia for single-firm investments.

insights.claim: The Dominican Republic's electronics exports rose 50% from 2018 to 2023, mostly from its 80-plus free trade zones, about 99% of whose output goes to the US.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: FTZ model is replicable; exposure is nearly all US.
insights.locator: The Dominican Republic seems to be learning

insights.claim: Latin America invested over $2 billion in data centers in 2024 and the market could double over four years; global demand is expected to grow 15% a year.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN

insights.claim: Brazil attracts over 40% of regional data center investment; its 800 MW capacity could reach 2 GW by 2030 and its incentive framework could draw $377 billion over a decade, helped by over 80% renewable electricity.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Clean power makes Brazil the regional AI-infrastructure favorite; watch incentive framework execution.
insights.locator: Global data center demand is expected to grow 15%

insights.claim: Querétaro drew $4.9 billion for six data centers last year, but Mexico lacks Brazil's clean-energy abundance; its 2025 electricity law fast-tracks industrial park generation, though progress will take time.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Power availability is Mexico's binding constraint for data centers.

insights.claim: The region's ICT services exports nearly doubled from 2020 to 2024, and ECLAC estimates AI contributed $70.7 billion, or 1.1% of regional GDP, in 2023.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.locator: Latin America's gains in hardware exports

insights.claim: Success factors are R&D investment, close public-private workforce coordination, IP protection, red-tape cuts, tax incentives and free trade zones, and scaling renewables paired with industrial projects.
insights.speaker: NUR CRISTIANI AND RICH BROWN
insights.so_what: Checklist for judging which countries can sustain the climb.
insights.locator: Adding value to the supply chain is within reach
